scopeReview: Aligned to IMP-1.A: reference/thematic maps, spatial patterns, absolute/relative distance and direction, clustering, elevation and selective projection distortion. No copied questions, named-country data or BC/other-subject content.
varietyReview: Four interpreted maps plus seven distinct applied/conceptual/data scenarios; all five geographic skills represented. Three foundational/intermediate entry points and demanding limitations/proportional-area questions. All four key positions used.
repetitionReview: No duplicate stems or shared numeric-only templates in this initial eleven-question set. No definition-only best-defines stem.

questions.correctOption: The two western districts have higher population densities than the eastern districts.
questions.independentReview: Recomputed west and east means from the four synthetic values: 80 versus 20. North and south means are both 50; no causal or total-population claim is needed.

questions.correctOption: Most mapped residents are concentrated in a northwest cluster.
questions.independentReview: Counted plotted points independently by quadrant: 12 northwest, 3 southeast, none elsewhere. Every point has the same 1,000-person value.

questions.correctOption: A steeper elevation gradient, because the same vertical change occurs over a shorter horizontal distance.
questions.independentReview: Compared 200/20 with 200/40 using labeled contour values and horizontal coordinates; west/east gradient ratio is 2. Projection/scale are held uniform by the hypothetical map definition.

questions.correctOption: B is 120 km due east of A in straight-line distance.
questions.independentReview: B=(80,15), A=(20,15); Δx=60, Δy=0. North-up means positive screen x is east, with distance 60×2=120 km.

questions.correctOption: An equal-area projection, while accepting that shapes or other properties will be distorted.
questions.independentReview: Checked the property demanded by the task: area, not shape/angles/distance. The claim is about projection properties rather than unsourced real-country measurements.

questions.correctOption: Their straight-line absolute distance stayed constant while their travel-time relative distance increased.
questions.independentReview: Separated fixed Euclidean separation from network travel-time impedance; no calculation or road geometry beyond the given times is assumed.

questions.correctOption: Comparing the spatial distribution of unemployment across provinces.
questions.independentReview: Matched each task to the explicitly described map information. No claim that all reference maps lack themes or that one map can never combine functions is made.

questions.correctOption: A province-wide summary can conceal variation among smaller areas.
questions.independentReview: Constructed a counterexample: a small high-rate neighborhood and a larger low-rate population can have a low weighted provincial rate. No inference about an individual is warranted.
Independently solved πrY²/(πrX²)=4. Positive radii give √4=2; distractor areas are 16, 256 and 1 times X.

questions.correctOption: Its near-current locations address an immediate travel decision that an annual regional average cannot resolve.
questions.independentReview: Compared the explicitly stated time supports and units of observation. Rejected the stronger claim that live points ensure a correct arrival forecast or complete information.

questions.correctOption: Their equality cannot be established from ruler lengths alone without accounting for spatially varying projection distortion.
questions.independentReview: The premise establishes nonuniform high-latitude stretching. Both unequal and differently scaled ground distances remain possible; the supported answer is insufficient evidence for equality.
